title: The Citizen Nexus
notes: The Citizen faction: what every Citizen Commander builds on. Its Grid Nexus, the Barracks and its troopers and marksmen (the engine's bench Citizen roster, named by id), the Supply Depot and the Garrison's tier (defined here), and the Nexus powers any Citizen Commander may be dealt. Choosing the Citizens' real roster and its balance is still to come (Milestone 12); every number is a first guess.

card.title: Garrison
card.subtitle: Trains pikemen
card.description: A heavier barracks. Trains a wave of pikemen, each worth about three troopers, a few seconds into each Battle Round.

content.notes: The tech tree's first second-tier building: the Barracks's bracket, heavier, closed walls where the Barracks's yard is open. Its pikemen appear on its roof and walk out over it, as a Barracks's troopers do.

card.title: Pikeman
card.subtitle: From your Garrison
card.description: Heavy infantry. Fights in melee like a trooper, and is worth about three of them.

content.notes: The Garrison's heavy infantry: about three troopers in health times damage, and two places of supply.

card.title: Supply Depot
card.subtitle: Room for 8 more units
card.description: Stores what an army needs to field more units at once. Your buildings stop training while the army is full.

content.notes: Supply as a building (the owner, 2026-10-16: "Supply should be controlled by another building"): eight more units the army may field at once.

card.title: Battery
card.subtitle: Trains mortars
card.description: A dug-in gun pit. Trains two mortars each Battle Round, once a Barracks stands.

content.notes: The mortar's building, of the second tier after the Barracks as the Garrison is: the Citizen bracket round a gun pit.

card.title: Mortar
card.subtitle: From your Battery
card.description: Slow artillery. Lobs a shell at the thickest knot of enemy troops in a long reach; the ground there burns for six seconds, hurting anyone on it, yours too. Never aims at a flyer or a building.

content.notes: The owner's yes, 2026-10-21: it stands back and lobs a shell at the thickest knot within a long reach. Half a trooper's pace (5/3), 30 health. Range 10: ten columns across, five rows up and down. One shell every 54 ticks (4.5 seconds at 12 a second), after a second's windup the first time, flying 2 columns a tick (5 ticks at full reach). The shell bursts for 8 within 2 and leaves the ground burning: 4 to every unit and worker within 4 of the impact, of either side, every second for six seconds (72 ticks), so a unit that stands in it all that time takes 24 and 32 with the burst, short of a trooper's 40. Routes weigh burning ground four times its ground, so a loose army walks round it. It aims at the enemy with the most of its side round it (aim: crowd), counted within the burn's radius. Two places of supply, as a pikeman. First numbers, to be measured.

buildings.notes: Four troopers in one wave a round, the owner's numbers (2026-10-05: 'Barraks could spawn 4 troops per round and that's is for now'). secondsBetween is unused while there is one wave; it is here for the day a Nexus power gives the Barracks a second and third wave.

Supply as a building: eight more units the army may field at once, where the Grid Nexus alone gives twelve. A building whose next unit would go past the supply waits, so once the army is full a new unit comes only as an old one falls (the power curve: survivors are outgrown). First guesses, no balance claim.

The tech tree's first second tier: it can be built once a Barracks stands as the Build Phase opens, so a Barracks placed this round unlocks it next round. Four pikemen a wave, as a Barracks sends four troopers, each about three troopers in health times damage, for two and a half times a Barracks's cost: a fifth better per credit, the power curve's guidance for a higher tier (commander-armies.md). First guesses, no balance claim.

Two mortars a wave once a Barracks stands, for a little more than a Barracks. A mortar's strength by the duel's measure (health times damage a second) is small, since most of its harm is the fire it leaves, so no scripted player picks it yet: a player chooses it against a tight army. First numbers, to be measured.

powers.name: Reserve Callup
powers.description: Two troopers join at your Nexus.
powers.notes: Units arrive: the two troopers are set down beside the Grid Nexus as the round's Battle Round starts, with the round's squads, and stay with the army after, coming home with Recall like any survivor. Repeatable: kept again, two more come. Twice as likely as another common in rounds 1 to 3 (the owner's example of a chance modifier, 2026-10-07: 'double chance during first 3 rounds'): troops matter most while the army is small.

powers.name: Drill Schedule
powers.notes: A building's waves, as the owner put it (2026-10-05): 'Nexus Powers could upgrade the Barracks to spawn a second and third wave.' Every Barracks spawns one more wave a round for the rest of the mission, its secondsBetween after the first. Kept once: its line says a second wave. Dealt only while a Barracks stands when the round opens: without one it would do nothing.

powers.name: Drill Schedule II
powers.notes: Drill Schedule's upgrade, the third wave of the owner's 'second and third wave': dealt only once Drill Schedule is kept, one rarity up, and listed in its place once kept. One more wave on top of Drill Schedule's, so every Barracks sends three.
